summary: The Federal Reserve held rates unchanged at 3.75-4.00% in a split 10-2 vote on October 28, with two hawkish dissents from Cook and Hammack pushing December hike odds to 83%. The decision was overshadowed by Thursday morning's macro data: Q3 GDP accelerated to 3.4% (vs 3.2% expected), and core PCE inflation held at 3.1%, reinforcing economic resilience while keeping pressure on the Fed to resume tightening. Meanwhile, Big Tech earnings delivered a stark divide—Alphabet plunged over 10% after its first revenue and profit miss in four years, dragging Nasdaq futures down 1%, while Microsoft rallied 3% on Azure strength. ServiceNow and Fortinet crashed 18% and 26% respectively, triggering a broad software sell-off. Bitcoin dropped below $80,000 after briefly touching $81,700, as spot ETF inflows of $137 million on Wednesday were overwhelmed by renewed risk-off sentiment and hawkish Fed tone. Markets face a key test today with Amazon, Intel, and Caterpillar earnings after the close.

signals.title: Fed holds with hawkish dissents, December hike odds jump to 83%
signals.desc: Two FOMC members voted for an immediate 25bp hike and Chair Warsh offered no dovish guidance, leaving the door open for tightening next meeting.

signals.title: Alphabet crashes 10% on first revenue/profit miss in four years
signals.desc: Google parent spent $9.1 billion more than it brought in via free cash flow, with search growth slowing despite strong cloud, dragging Nasdaq futures down 1%.

signals.title: Q3 GDP beats at 3.4%, core PCE in-line at 3.1%
signals.desc: Stronger-than-expected growth and stable inflation support the resilience narrative, but also justify further Fed hawkishness.

signals.title: Bitcoin falls below $80k as spot ETF inflows fade after three-day streak
signals.desc: BTC dropped from $81,700 to sub-$80,000 as hawkish Fed tone and tech weakness trigger $356M in leveraged liquidations, mostly longs.

signals.title: Software stocks collapse: ServiceNow -18%, Fortinet -26% post-earnings
signals.desc: ServiceNow missed guidance and Fortinet cut forecasts, sparking a sector-wide rout and pulling down cybersecurity names CRWD and PANW by 6%.

verdict: Hawkish Fed, hot GDP, and Big Tech carnage point to a risk-off open with tech under pressure while defensives and the dollar hold steady.
